bib.title: Teaching LLMs to Plan: Logical Chain-of-Thought Instruction Tuning for Symbolic Planning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Teaching LLMs to Plan: Logical Chain-of-Thought Instruction Tuning for Symbolic Planning" (PDDL-INSTRUCT). Pulkit Verma, Ngoc La, Anthony Favier, Swaroop Mishra, Julie A. Shah. arXiv 2509.13351v1, 14 Sep 2025. Preprint (no venue printed).

COVERAGE: 92,072 of 92,072 chars read, covering the main text, limitations, and appendices A-C (hyperparameters, losses, algorithm, prompts, ablation table, error table). The reference list was skimmed. The extraction was clean.

FIT WARNING FOR THE TARGET NOTE: This is a fine-tuning paper on PDDL/STRIPS planning, not prompting or tool-use. It has no tool-choice experiments, no DAG plans, and no agentic tool calls. Only weak links exist:
- (a) an external verifier (VAL) is the only feedback;
- (b) the model must restate the state after every action;
- (c) the plan names its actions with preconditions and effects.
Do not cite it for "choosing among many tools" or "plans as DAGs". The plan format is a linear sequence (STRIPS, satisficing plans).

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Claim: Logical-CoT instruction tuning with external VAL feedback lifts plan validity far above untuned models. Llama-3-8B reaches 94% on Blocksworld, 64% on Mystery Blocksworld and 79% on Logistics.
  number: 94% / 64% / 79%, against baselines of 28% / 1% / 11%. GPT-4: 91% / 59% / 78%, against baselines of 35% / 3% / 6%.
  setup: PlanBench, 3 domains, 100 test tasks per domain, plan validity checked by VAL. Detailed feedback, eta=15. Single generation at test time with no feedback returned. Baseline is the unmodified model (prompt not specified). Differences are in absolute percentage points.
  quote: "For Llama-3, PDDL-INSTRUCT with detailed feedback and η= 15 achieves validity rates of 94%, 64%, and 79%, respectively in Blocksworld, Mystery Blocksworld, and Logistics."
  where: p.7, about char 25,000
- Claim: The average absolute gains are 66 points (SD 3) over the baseline and 35 points (SD 20) over Phase-1-only tuning for Llama-3. For GPT-4 they are 61 (SD 9) and 48 (SD 5). I checked these against Table 1 and they are consistent.
  number: 35% / 66%; 48% / 61%
  setup: as above, averaged over the three domains.
  quote: "represents an average absolute improvement of 35%(SD= 20%) over basic instruction tuning, and of 66%(SD= 3%) over the baseline."
  where: p.8
- Claim: Detailed feedback (which precondition failed or which effect was wrong) beats binary valid/invalid feedback in every domain and model.
  number: Llama-3, eta=15, gain of 5 pts in Blocksworld, 15 pts in Mystery BW and 7 pts in Logistics. Table 1: 89 vs 94, 49 vs 64, 72 vs 79.
  setup: same as above; the feedback was used during training, not at test time.
  quote: "For Llama-3 with η= 15 , detailed feedback improves plan accuracy by 5 percentage points in Blocksworld, 15 percentage points in Mystery Blocksworld, and 7 percentage points in Logistics compared to binary feedback."
  where: p.8
- Claim: Both phases are needed. Phase 1 only gives 78 / 32 / 23. Phase 2 only gives 72 / 17 / 45. Both together give 94 / 64 / 79.
  number: see Table 4.
  setup: Llama-3, detailed feedback, eta=15. Table 4 gives ± values (e.g. 94.0±1.5) but the text does not say what they are across (seeds?).
  quote: "Phase 1 + Detailed Feedback (η= 15)94.0±1.5 64.0±3.8 79.0±3.2"
  where: Appendix C.1, Table 4
- Claim: More feedback iterations help a little. Going from eta=10 to 15 adds an average of 4.3 pts with detailed feedback and 3.3 pts with binary. The authors say they need more experiments to confirm convergence.
  number: 4.3 / 3.3 points
  quote: "The improvement is more substantial with detailed feedback (averaging 4.3 percentage points across all domains and models) than with binary feedback (averaging 3.3 percentage points)"
  where: p.8
- Claim: Remaining failures are mostly wrong effect application and precondition violations, concentrated in the obfuscated domain.
  number: Mystery BW 36.0% total failure, of which incorrect effect application is 12.4%. Logistics 21.0%. Blocksworld 6.0%.
  setup: Llama-3, Phase 1+2, detailed feedback, eta=15 (Table 5). The rows sum to the totals.
  quote: "Incorrect Effect Application 1.4 12.4 6.8"
  where: Appendix C.2, Table 5
- Claim: Cost. Training takes 30 hours in total (12 for Phase 1 and 18 for Phase 2) on 2x 24GB GPUs, and inference takes 2.3 s per problem.
  quote: "Total Training Time 30 hours"
  where: Table 3, Appendix A.4
- Claim (design, no number): The model must write out, per action, the preconditions checked, the effects applied (add and delete lists) and the resulting full state, then run a goal check. This is the "restate state" pattern. The authors argue that an external verifier avoids the weakness of LLM self-critique.
  quote: "while some approaches have tried using LLMs themselves as verifiers, research shows that currently LLMs do not possess sufficient self-correction capabilities in terms of reasoning"
  where: p.5
- Claim: The authors say the approach reduces the problem of unfaithful CoT because every step is checked by VAL.
  quote: "A notable advantage of our VAL-based verification approach is its robustness against unfaithful chain-of-thought reasoning"
  where: p.9. This is an assertion, not tested.

BASELINE MATCHING: The baselines are neither compute-matched nor call-matched.
- The baseline is the untuned model, with no training and no feedback loop. Training used up to 10-15 VAL feedback iterations plus 30 GPU-hours.
- There is no comparison against few-shot CoT prompting, sampling plus VAL filtering at test time, or a classical planner.
- The test-time comparison is one generation per problem, so token cost per problem differs (CoT chains of up to 2048 generated tokens against a plain baseline).
- The "Phase 1 only" ablation is the closest tuned control.
- The abstract's "66% absolute improvement" is the Llama-3 average gain over the untuned baseline.

LIMITS
- Only 3 PlanBench domains with 100 tasks each. No per-problem-size breakdown. The ± in Table 4 is unexplained. Table 1 gives no CIs.
- Only Llama-3-8B and GPT-4. The GPT-4 setup is unclear, since the paper says only that "GPT-4 experiments were constrained by limited access". How GPT-4 was tuned is not described.
- STRIPS subset only: no conditional effects, durative actions or costs. Satisficing plans only, with no optimality.
- Training and test appear to be from the same domains, yet the paper claims "domain-general" transfer. No held-out-domain experiment is described. Treat the generalization claim as weak.
- It does not reach 100%, and Mystery BW tops out at 64%.
- The authors concede that the effect of eta is unconfirmed ("future experiments with varying η are needed").
- The prior work they cite found self-iterative feedback degrades performance. Here VAL is used only in training, and no test-time verifier loop is evaluated. They suggest combining with LLM-Modulo.
- The training prompt data: the "Phase 1 ... explain why each action is valid" prompt is also used for invalid plans.

BUILDS ON: PlanBench (Valmeekam et al., 2023b); VAL validator (Howey et al., 2004); PDDL (McDermott et al., 1998) and STRIPS (Fikes and Nilsson, 1971); chain-of-thought (Wei et al., 2022b); instruction tuning (Mishra et al., 2022; Wei et al., 2022a; Ouyang et al., 2022); NaturalInstructions-style data (Wang et al., 2022); LLM-Modulo (Kambhampati et al., 2024); critiques that CoT and self-verification fail for planning (Stechly et al., 2024; Stechly et al., 2025; Valmeekam et al., 2023a; Huang et al., 2024). They note independent similarity to LEPA (Zhang et al., 2025a) and NL2P (Gestrin et al., 2024).

CODE: No code was released in the text. The Appendix B prompt template (p.23) shows the restate-state format:
"[Step 1: State s0 Action a1 State s1]
- Current state s0: (on c b), (ontable b), (ontable a), (clear c), (clear a), (handempty)
- Proposed action a1: (pick-up a)
- Precondition check:
- (clear a): TRUE in s0 ... - Action is APPLICABLE
- Effect application: - Add: (holding a) - Delete: (ontable a), (handempty), (clear a)
- Resulting state s1: (on c b), (ontable b), (clear c), (holding a)"
The same prompt ends with "[GOAL ACHIEVEMENT CHECK]" and "[FINAL PLAN]".
Loss in Appendix A.2: L_step = d_state(s_i, s_expected) + λ·L_feedback, with λ_feedback = 0.1, α_precond = 1.0, α_effect = 1.0, α_goal = 1.5 (eq. 5-7).
Algorithm 1 (p.19): loop up to eta times: generate CoT plan, validate with VAL, collect (state, action, state, feedback) triples, then tune in two stages (reasoning loss, then final loss).

FIGURES: Fig. 1 (p.2) is the pipeline diagram: Phase 1 initial tuning, Phase 2 CoT tuning with VAL binary or detailed feedback, and an evaluation phase with no feedback. It is the one candidate figure. I did not run the captions script. The Table 1 numbers are better shown as a small table.

PROBLEMS:
- No embedded instructions were found in the PDF.
- Table 1 column headers extracted garbled (Baseline, Only P1, Only P2, then Binary eta=10 and 15, Detailed eta=10 and 15). I reconstructed the order from the first row (28/78/72/84/89/91/94) and Table 4, which matches.
- The appendix reads as partly formulaic. The hyperparameter prose is long, and it is unclear whether the Phase 2 "loss" with BCE on predicted validity matches what was actually implemented.
- The results in the main text are single-point values with no variance, except Table 4.
- The extracted text is at /tmp/verma.txt (temporary).
